transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you too. 

Well, I came in because... lately I just can't seem to stop focusing on my appearance. At work, I recently started helping out with the safety trainings. But when I'm up there pointing things out, I just can't stop noticing how wrinkly and uneven my hands look. It really bothers me. 

And then... well, they put some photos of the trainings in the company newsletter, and when I look at them, I start thinking my face looks crooked. I've mentioned it to other people, but they tell me they don't see it at all. I just can't seem to let it go, though, and it's been getting on my nerves.
When you are feeling bothered by these thoughts about your hands or your face, do you find yourself doing anything specific to try to fix, hide, or check them?

Yeah, I suppose I do. Before I have to do a class at work, or even a workshop down at the senior center, I'll usually go check the bathroom mirror a few times. I make sure to put lotion on my hands, and I'll turn my face different ways in the mirror just to see how it looks. Sometimes I'll even ask a coworker if I look all right, just to get their opinion. Doing all that... well, it makes me run a little behind schedule sometimes, but I still get myself there.
How much time out of your day would you say you spend thinking about these perceived flaws or performing these mirror-checking and reassurance-seeking behaviors?

I'm not exactly sure if I've ever sat down and timed it, to be honest. It's just something that pops into my head throughout the day, especially when I know people are going to be looking at me. Maybe a few minutes here and there when I'm checking the mirror or putting on lotion. It doesn't take over my whole day, but it's just... there, you know? Enough to be annoying.
How much does this preoccupation with your appearance negatively affect your daily life, such as your job performance, your social interactions, or your ability to get things done?

Well, it hasn't stopped me from doing my job or volunteering at the senior center. I still get everything done. But... I am definitely slower getting ready for those trainings because of all the mirror checking. And I've started ducking out of the way if someone has a camera around, which I didn't use to do. I guess I also hesitate a bit more before going to social events. I still go, but it takes a little more effort to get out the door than it used to.

The symptoms are clinically significant but do not currently meet the threshold for higher severity or other disorders.
